body:
READ-ONLY MOTE SOURCE AUDIT — compatibility patch state and reconciliation authority; no edit, build, install, store write, or candidate operation.

Current /Users/bbuchsbaum/code/rust/mote is HEAD 2f38536, ahead one, with unattributed dirty changes in exactly src/candidate.rs and tests/candidate_protocol.rs plus an unrelated untracked Claude lock. The source diff adds skip_serializing_if for relation_schema == 1 and a focused legacy-digest/omitted-field/v2-explicit regression. It matches m1's independently proven serde repair. I am not attributing it to the exited Cargo PID or calling it complete: it still lacks the chief-required real historical review reattachment observation, copied-full-store accepted/rejected equivalence, mutation death in the actual crate, full candidate protocol, cargo test, fmt, clippy, immutable commit, and patched-binary receipt.

Authority trace:
- CandidateReconciliationAuthority has exactly ProposalAuthorizer.
- CLI rejects before probing unless candidate.authorizer == actor.
- Reducer records only that variant.
- A separate SuccessorAuthorizerContainment authority already exists, but only for candidate_supersede, where the terminal meaning is superseded. Reusing that command on a commit already reachable from main would record a false state and must not be done.
- FORMAT.json has no store owner, and this store has zero first-class roles. Therefore an ambient chief, recent actor, repository owner, lease, or board-prose inference has no deterministic authority root today.

Safest typed extension to consider: add SuccessorAuthorizerContainment as an explicit candidate_reconcile authority, not an ambient owner override. The op would name a distinct successor candidate, both phase CAS values, exact current containment evidence op ids, and both policy snapshots; reducer would require same store/landing repository/object format/entity, complete determinate predecessor.tip -> successor.tip ancestry, successor.authorizer == actor, and a successor policy that is otherwise review/evidence/authorization-complete except for ancestor blockers caused by the predecessor being repaired. It would still terminalize the predecessor as landed_out_of_band, preserving the true Git fact and its original governance snapshot; it would not transfer reviews or call the old landing governed. The audit record would name the successor authority and containment basis.

A store-owner/deputy override is a different protocol and currently has no machine-readable root of trust; adding one safely requires explicit owner authority plus a new immutable delegation/role policy rather than accepting a caller-selected actor or discussion post. Chief should choose that larger root only with direct owner authorization.

This is a design finding, not implementation authority. It avoids both impersonating claude-storymodel4s and misusing supersede.
